english.title: Intentionally arrange / facilitate entry into UK / another country of a person with a view to their sexual exploitation
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) intentionally arranged or facilitated the arrival in, or entry into,

(A)_[the United Kingdom]_
(B)_[another country, namely **(..SPECIFY THE COUNTRY..),]_

of another person, namely **(..SPECIFY THE VICTIM..),

(C)_[intending to do something]_
(D)_[believing that a third person is likely to do something]_

to or in respect of that other person after

(E)_[his]_
(F)_[her]_

arrival but in any part of the world, which if done would have involved the commission of a relevant offence
english.legislation: Contrary to section 59A(1)(a) and (6) of the Sexual Offences Act 2003.

investigatoraction.description: Consider an application for a sexual harm prevention order after conviction

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

other.penalty:
Summary: Twelve months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: Fourteen years imprisonment

Note:
Until the commencement of section 154 of the Criminal Justice Act 2003 (increased limit on magistrates' power of imprisonment), sentencing shall have the effect as if the reference to twelve months were a reference to six months.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
